text:
Alex C: just pushed NF4 -> canary pool at 08:12, seeing a throughput dip on long sequences (seq_len>1024) and a memory bump on 3 nodes :thinking_face:
Priya S: same, p95 token latency up ~22% on the canary set. baseline (fp16) vs nf4_v3 kernel swap looks correlated.
Marcus T: from quick perf: kernel selector chose `4bit_nf4_opt_v3` for longer requests which uses new packing path. KV cache eviction count spiked.
Jenna L: can you paste the perf counters or logs? want to check batching shape and KV hit rate.
Marcus T: pasted small snippet:
```
[2026-03-18T08:14:05Z] model=rwkv-nf4 kernel=4bit_nf4_opt_v3 seq=1536 batch=2 tokens/sec=4200 mem_used=78GB kv_evictions=712
[2026-03-18T08:14:10Z] model=rwkv-nf4 kernel=4bit_nf4_opt_v3 seq=1536 batch=4 tokens/sec=3600 mem_used=84GB kv_evictions=1201
```
Priya S: kv_evictions jump is the red flag. I think the new kernel increases dense KV footprint per layer (maybe different alignment).
Alex C: deploy-bot shows autoscaler triggered extra pods then OOMs on one canary node.
deploy-bot: "canary-deploy nf4-v3 started (id: cd3f). autoscale: +2 pods, pod nf4-canary-3 restarted due to OOM"
Marcus T: I ran a small profiling session with heap snapshots and saw slab fragmentation in allocator after kernel load. flamegraph attached in thread (uploaded).
Jenna L: suggestion: temporarily pin canary to fallback kernel `4bit_nf4_compat_v2` and run a memory-focused microbench: seq=1536, batch sweep 1..8, measure kv hits.
Alex C: agreed. quick mitigation: change kernel routing policy for canary to prefer `compat_v2` until we root cause. Also reduce max_batch_bytes to lower KV working set.
Priya S: also test alternative batching heuristic — current continuous-batch groups requests up to 6 if latency goal <200ms. For long seqs that pushes mem over limit. Try cap_batches_for_long_seq = 2.
Marcus T: repro steps I used:
```
# run against canary backend
curl -X POST https://canary.redwood/api/generate -d '{"model":"rwkv-nf4","seq_len":1536,"batch_size":4,"prompt":"<L>"}'
# monitor kv metrics
kubectl logs -l app=rwkv-canary -c runtime --tail=200 | grep kv_evictions
```
Jenna L: can we get a cheap perf counter: KV average entry size per layer? that would confirm if packing changed.
Marcus T: `rwkv-profiler --dump-kv-stats` output:
```
layer0: avg_entry=256 bytes, entries=2048
layer12: avg_entry=384 bytes, entries=1984 (compat_v2)
layer12: avg_entry=512 bytes, entries=1984 (opt_v3)
```
Priya S: that explains the mem jump. opt_v3 increases avg_entry for some layers (pack + alignment). Combined with batching, working set crosses GPU memory threshold -> evictions -> latency.
Alex C: plan: 1) rollback kernel selector on canary to compat_v2 (today) 2) ramp max_batch_bytes down and cap batches for seq>1024 (short term) 3) run microbench across kernels to collect avg_entry histograms and allocator fragmentation (next 24h) 4) fix kernel packing or adjust allocator alignment (investigation).
Jenna L: I'll open an infra ticket to reserve extra headroom on a sandbox cluster for deep perf tests (can't run on prod canary due to risk).
Marcus T: I'll run a calibration sweep to check if quant calibration interacts (we saw some accuracy drift when switching alignments). Might be a compaction pass issue.
Priya S: note for release notes: mention kernel opt_v3 increases per-layer KV footprint for certain model shapes. We should include recommended batch caps.
Alex C: thanks all. I'm pinning canary to compat_v2 now and will post once rollback is live. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: "routing override applied: prefer 4bit_nf4_compat_v2 for canary pool (cd3f)."
Alex C: rollback confirmed, initial metrics show latency dropping back and kv_evictions flattening. We'll keep this thread for follow-ups on allocator changes and kernel packing fixes.
Jenna L: filing follow-up doc with perf plots and allocator dumps.
Marcus T: will upload the full profiler output and a short reproduce harness tomorrow.
Priya S: thanks, labeling as P1 canary perf regression for tracking.
Alex C: end.
